as_written_in_papers.quote: Genetic testing revealed two pathogenic variants in GAMT: c.268G>C (p.Glu90Gln) and c.522G>A (p.Trp174*) variants.

cases.statement: One person: Patient 2 of 40330029, a 21-year-old woman diagnosed at 12.5 years, carrying c.268G>C (p.Glu90Gln) and c.522G>A (p.Trp174*).

people.label: Patient 2
people.zygosity_or_genotype: two GAMT variants; phase not reported
people.key_phenotypes: intractable epilepsy from age 3, global developmental delay, autism, no expressive language, wide-based gait; seizures resolved on creatine and ornithine

quotes.quote: Patient 2: Patient 2 is a 21‐year‐old female who was diagnosed with GAMT deficiency at 12.5 years old.
She presented with intractable epilepsy, global developmental delay, and autism.
At presentation, she had no expressive language, limited eye contact, wide‐based gait, and significant behavioral concerns.
She started having intermittent seizures at 3 years old that continued to worsen, despite multiple antiseizure c medications.
Within 6 months of treatment, seizures resolved and all antiseizur medications were weaned.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Intractable epilepsy, global developmental delay and autism, typical of the disease as the paper describes it, with a marked clinical response to creatine and ornithine. Pre-treatment GAA/creatine values are given only in a figure; post-treatment GAA remained above reference. Testing method and exclusion of other genes are not reported.

quotes.quote: She presented with intractable epilepsy, global developmental delay, and autism.
Within 6 months of treatment, seizures resolved and all antiseizur medications were weaned.
Her post‐treatment average GAA and creatine were 6.6 μM/L (reference range 0.3–2.1 μM/L) and 935 μM/L (reference range 20–110 μM/L), respectively (Figure 1).
Her pre‐treatment severity score was 6, decreasing to 3 post‐treatment.

in_trans.statement: Other allele c.522G>A (p.Trp174*). Phase is not reported (no parental testing described).

quotes.quote: Genetic testing revealed two pathogenic variants in GAMT: c.268G>C (p.Glu90Gln) and c.522G>A (p.Trp174*) variants.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, predicted p.(Glu90Gln) (from the HGVS). The paper describes the disease as autosomal recessive due to biallelic pathogenic variants; no mechanism statement specific to this variant.

quotes.quote: has since been characterized as an autosomal recessive condition secondary to biallelic pathogenic variants in GAMT (OMIM *601240).

authors_classification.statement: The authors call both variants 'pathogenic', without ACMG criteria.

quotes.quote: Genetic testing revealed two pathogenic variants in GAMT: c.268G>C (p.Glu90Gln) and c.522G>A (p.Trp174*) variants.

concerns: Phase of c.268G>C and c.522G>A is not shown; no parental testing is reported.
The authors' 'pathogenic' label is given without criteria, evidence or a source.
The genetic test used (panel, exome) is not described, so other causes are not shown to be excluded.
notes_for_panel: Single affected person; missense variant with no segregation, phase, functional, computational or population data in the paper. 42885896 lists only Lee 2025 Pt 3 (not Pt 2) in its adult table, so this person does not reappear there.
